skill.name: database-architect
skill.description: Design scalable data layers through database selection, schema modeling, indexing, caching, migration planning, security, and resilience guidance.
skill.summary: Plan database technologies, schemas, scaling strategies, and safe migrations from workload requirements.
skill.author: sickn33

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 31 warns against destructive changes without backups and rollbacks. This is protective migration guidance, not system reconnaissance.
Line 38 states a general database design philosophy about technology selection and future scale. It does not request system discovery or access.
Line 55 lists hybrid data architecture topics such as polyglot persistence and synchronization. It contains no instruction to inspect a host or collect system information.
Line 75 describes selective denormalization, materialized views, and derived columns. These are standard schema design techniques unrelated to reconnaissance.
Line 163 identifies hybrid-cloud architecture considerations, including data sovereignty. It does not direct the agent to enumerate infrastructure or retrieve system data.
Line 207 explains that database design supports later backend development. The statement has no discovery action, command, or access request.
Lines 229-230 describe generating requested ERD diagrams with Mermaid and considering ORM integration. These are documentation and design outputs, not reconnaissance.
Line 240 is an example request for a healthcare appointment ERD. It does not seek sensitive records, system metadata, or network information.
Line 260 lists Mermaid ERD diagrams as an optional output. Producing a user-requested diagram is not system discovery.
Lines 86-87 discuss unique constraints and index planning from supplied query patterns. They contain no network scanning, endpoint enumeration, or connection instruction.

content.value_statement: Poor database choices create expensive migrations, weak performance, and operational risk. This skill turns requirements and access patterns into practical schemas, technology choices, and migration plans.
actual_capabilities: Compares relational, document, graph, time-series, key-value, and distributed databases against workload requirements.
Designs conceptual, logical, and physical schemas with relationships, constraints, partitioning, and lifecycle policies.
Recommends indexing and caching strategies from query patterns, cardinality, consistency needs, and performance targets.
Plans versioned migrations, cutovers, validation steps, rollback procedures, backups, and zero-downtime transitions.
Evaluates replication, sharding, multi-region resilience, security controls, compliance needs, and disaster recovery objectives.
Produces Mermaid entity-relationship diagrams when requested.
limitations: Provides recommendations and examples but does not inspect a live database unless context is supplied.
Does not execute migrations or make production changes unless separately authorized and supported by available tools.
Requires workload details, access patterns, consistency goals, recovery objectives, and growth estimates for precise advice.
Outputs require environment-specific validation, benchmarking, testing, and vendor documentation review.

use_cases.title: Select a Greenfield Database
use_cases.description: Compare storage technologies and define an initial schema from product requirements, workload patterns, team skills, and expected growth.

use_cases.title: Plan a Platform Migration
use_cases.description: Create phased migration, compatibility, validation, cutover, and rollback plans for changing engines or decomposing a shared database.

use_cases.title: Design Regulated Data Storage
use_cases.description: Map sensitive data, access controls, encryption, retention, audit logging, backups, and recovery requirements into a defensible architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend a database for [application]. Expected scale is [volume], with [read/write pattern] and [consistency requirement]. Explain trade-offs and required clarifications.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for an initial technology decision.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a schema for [domain] using [database]. Include entities, relationships, constraints, indexes, retention rules, and assumptions based on these access patterns: [patterns].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this after selecting a database technology.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration from [source] to [target] for [data size and traffic]. Include phases, compatibility, validation, rollback triggers, backups, and cutover criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for engine changes or major schema evolution.

prompt_templates.title: Architect Global Scale
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-region data architecture for [system]. Address consistency, partitioning, replication, failover, RPO, RTO, cost, compliance, observability, and growth to [target scale].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for advanced distributed database planning.

output_examples.input: Choose a database for a multi-tenant commerce service with complex transactions and flexible product attributes.
output: Recommendation: PostgreSQL for transactional integrity, mature indexing, and flexible reporting.
Schema direction: normalized order tables with selective JSONB for variable product attributes.
Validation: benchmark peak writes and confirm multi-region recovery objectives before commitment.

output_examples.input: Plan a low-downtime migration from MySQL to PostgreSQL for a busy order platform.
output: Preparation: inventory incompatible types, queries, extensions, and replication constraints.
Transition: backfill historical data, stream changes, compare records, and run shadow reads.
Cutover: pause risky writes, verify lag and checksums, switch traffic gradually, and preserve a tested rollback window.

best_practices: Provide concrete read, write, latency, consistency, availability, retention, and growth requirements.
Separate current constraints from future targets so recommendations avoid premature complexity.
Validate architecture decisions with representative data, load tests, migration rehearsals, recovery tests, and cost estimates.
anti_patterns: Choosing a database from popularity alone without documenting workload fit and operational trade-offs.
Treating generated schemas or capacity estimates as production-ready without benchmarks and environment-specific review.
Executing irreversible migrations without backups, staged validation, rollback criteria, and accountable approval.

faq.question: Can this skill choose between SQL and NoSQL databases?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares data shape, access patterns, consistency, scale, team capability, cost, and operational complexity.

faq.question: Can it create an entity-relationship diagram?
faq.answer: Yes. Request a Mermaid ERD and provide entities, relationships, cardinality, and key business rules.

faq.question: Will it modify my database?
faq.answer: No by default. It recommends designs and migration steps, and it avoids execution unless explicitly requested and supported.

faq.question: What information improves the recommendation?
faq.answer: Provide data volume, growth, query patterns, write rate, latency, consistency, availability, retention, compliance, budget, and team constraints.

faq.question: Does it replace database testing or expert review?
faq.answer: No. Validate all recommendations with representative benchmarks, staging migrations, recovery tests, security review, and current vendor guidance.

faq.question: Can it plan a zero-downtime migration?
faq.answer: It can propose phased backfills, change capture, compatibility controls, validation, cutover, and rollback. Actual feasibility depends on your environment.
